source_binding.line_format_verified: L######## followed by tab and exact canonical source text

items.title: Checkpoint authority is correctly separated
items.statement: The source explicitly separates projector durability checkpoints from runtime recovery markers and requires both for mutation/recovery replay. This closes a common authority-confusion failure mode.
items.impact: Projectors cannot silently become the authority for resuming mutation-capable runtime work.

evidence.exact_quote:
projector checkpoints are not a substitute for runtime recovery checkpoint markers. Runtime/executor-owned checkpoint marker events and safe-point lineage records MUST be durably emitted to seglog before mutation-capable execution resumes or restore flows continue.
- recovery resume logic uses the canonical runtime checkpoint marker stream plus projector checkpoints; projector checkpoints alone are insufficient for mutation/recovery replay.

items.title: Analytics window and checkpoint contract can produce stale or inconsistent rollups
items.statement: The canonical windows include 24h, but computation is specified only for 5h/7d; the checkpoint may be either sequence or timestamp despite sequence being the replay authority. The contract also does not say how sliding-window expirations are recomputed when no new events arrive or when a JSONL mirror lags seglog.
items.impact: Independent builders can omit 24h, skip or double-count events at timestamp boundaries, and leave dashboard totals stale while still satisfying the prose.

evidence.exact_quote:
**Scan range:** Last N hours (e.g. at least 7d for `tool_usage.7d`) or since last scan checkpoint. Read from seglog (or JSONL mirror) in order; filter by event type (`usage.event`, `run.completed`, `tool.invoked`). Canonical tool-usage windows for MVP are `5h`, `24h`, and `7d`; `1h` remains optional.

**Compute:** For 5h/7d: aggregate `usage.event` by platform, sum tokens (or request count) in sliding 5h and 7d windows. For tool latency: collect `tool.invoked` latencies, compute percentiles (p50, p95). For error rates: count run failures / total runs in window. For **tool usage** (Usage tool widget, Plans/Tools.md §8.4): aggregate `tool.invoked` by `tool_name` over the window -- count, p50/p95 ms, error_count (count only events where `success = false`). `tool.denied` events and FileSafe blocks do **not** contribute to `tool_usage.{window}` because the widget reflects executed calls only.

**Write:** Store results in redb under `rollups` namespace (e.g. `usage_5h.{platform}`, `usage_7d.{platform}`, `tool_latency.{window}`, **`tool_usage.{window}`**, `tool_usage_meta.{window}`). Usage view and tool usage widget read from these keys; no direct seglog read for dashboard.

**Checkpoint:** Store "last scanned up to seq X" or "last scanned timestamp" in redb so the next run doesn't rescan from the beginning. Idempotent: recomputing the same window and writing the same keys is safe.

items.title: Absent worktree context silently becomes main-project context
items.statement: A background enqueue from a bound thread may omit both worktree fields, and consumers are instructed to interpret absence as main-project context. There is no invariant binding the enqueue record to the thread binding snapshot or preventing mutation in the wrong tree.
items.impact: A partial producer payload can redirect background work from an isolated worktree to the main project without an explicit downgrade or block.

evidence.exact_quote: `run.background_enqueued` remains part of the existing run-event family and may carry optional `worktree_path` and `branch_name` fields when background work is enqueued from a bound thread. Consumers treat absent fields as main-project context rather than inventing worktree context.

items.title: Question persistence mixes status dimensions and slash aliases
items.statement: The source declares one canonical terminal-status enum, then a second flow-state vocabulary containing both `draft` and `/draft` plus another `submitted`. It does not define whether these are separate dimensions, legal transitions, precedence after timeout/dismissal, or reload behavior for validation failures.
items.impact: Storage and GUI consumers can persist mutually incompatible states and render a draft as submitted or resumable after a terminal outcome.

evidence.exact_quote:
Question and questionnaire persistence stores thread-scoped draft state, answer state, and final submission state as bounded structured data only, without inventing chat-local aliases. Canonical status values are `answered | submitted | dismissed | timed_out | unavailable`; `draft_value`, `response_kind`, and `validation_state` persist with the question item so reloads can resume a partially answered `/questionnaire` flow.

Shared question-card persistence covers single-question and multi-question flows with explicit `draft`, `/draft`, `incomplete`, `ready_to_submit`, `submitted`, and `paused` states. Composer controls may expose `/send` and `/resend`, but storage records only the state transition and active-run linkage needed to rewind later work, pause follow, or restore jump-to-latest context.

items.title: TODO revision rule cannot be reconstructed from the event schema
items.statement: Post-execution edits must create a new revision event, but the locked minimal `chat.plan_todo_updated` payload has no revision ID, parent revision, plan revision, ordering sequence, or approval snapshot. Old/new values typed as `any` also leave schema evolution and redaction unconstrained.
items.impact: Replay cannot deterministically reconstruct bounded revision history or prove that an approved plan was not mutated in place.

evidence.exact_quote:
Durable TODO mutation events persist `chat.plan_todo_updated` with minimal payload schema `{ plan_id: string, todo_id: string, field: string, old_value: any, new_value: any, source: "agent" | "user" }`. Storage retains `plan_id`, `todo_id`, changed `field`, `old_value`, `new_value`, and mutation `source` so replay can distinguish agent edits from user edits.
- The Assistant chat plan panel remains the `/source-of-truth` for visible TODO execution state, while storage owns the durable normalized TODO projection. `/todo/tool` activity, `todoread`, `todowrite`, question cards, web activity cards, assistant runtime disclosures, and other `/consumer` surfaces all obey the same persistence boundary.
- User edits and reorder operations are pre-approval structural changes. After execution begins, reorder or status corrections create a new TODO revision event instead of mutating the approved plan in place.

items.title: Bridge-field precedence is required but not defined
items.statement: The activity payload names local attempt identity, provider references, effective account identity, and inspection refs, then says precedence must be explicit without supplying a precedence table or mismatch behavior.
items.impact: Audit, usage, artifacts, and GUI consumers can disagree about which identity wins when bridge fields conflict or are stale.

evidence.exact_quote:
Behavioral rules:
- Inspection refs remain inspection/provenance refs; route/open contracts remain route/open contracts.
- Bridge-field precedence must be explicit rather than inferred.

items.title: Persisted visual modules lack a security and data-lifecycle contract
items.statement: Version pinning and integrity are required for third-party scripts, but the storage contract does not define origin binding, secret/PII scrubbing, retention, revocation after a library becomes disallowed, or safe behavior when re-rendering old untrusted source under a newer runtime.
items.impact: Reload/export can re-execute stored hostile or privacy-sensitive HTML/JS/CSS despite the host bridge being nominally sandboxed.

evidence.exact_quote:
Inline visualizer persistence stores the source fragment as an `HTML/JS/CSS` string, including richer `/JS` visuals, plus render config such as width, height, `/design` theme tokens, `/auto-height` constraints, and bridge metadata for the sandboxed `visual-module` card.
- Bridge metadata records only approved host-mediated capabilities such as the `open-link` bridge and local `in-module` visual state refs; arbitrary bridge calls, direct DOM reach-through, and client heap state are not durable storage.
- Question-flow embedded visuals persist explicit PM-managed draft-state outputs instead of generic `send-message` bridge payloads, so reloads resume the question draft lifecycle without converting draft answers into chat messages.
- `/interactive` visual modules may record bundled `/scripts` or third-party library refs only when the supported visual runtime has version-pinned, integrity-recorded, and policy-allowed them as part of the visual source metadata.
- Rendered output references may include screenshot or `/snapshot` fallback evidence for scroll-back; on thread reload/export review, PM re-renders from the persisted source fragment, title/type metadata, render config, and PM-managed state outputs, and uses the screenshot fallback only when re-render is impractical.

items.title: Unsaved recovery identity and retention remain underspecified
items.statement: The required snapshot includes host/path identity and remote write availability, but the key includes only project ID and file-path hash. The hash input, collision handling, host disambiguation, encryption/retention of unsaved content, and cleanup after save/discard are not defined.
items.impact: Two host-backed files can collide or restore into the wrong destination, and sensitive unsaved buffers can persist indefinitely.

evidence.exact_quote:
recover-unsaved is required MVP behavior for local and remote-backed buffers
- recovery snapshots store local buffer state, capture metadata, host/path identity, and write availability at capture time
- remote-backed recovery banners must say `Recovered local edits — remote destination not yet synchronized`
- save success is only claimed after the effective destination confirms the write

Implementation spec:
- key: `editor_state.v1:{project_id}:{file_path_hash}`
- stores: cursor position, scroll offset, selection ranges, undo stack reference, and unsaved changes flag
- recovery trigger: on session restore, reload each open editor's state before restoring focus
- conflict handling: if the file changed on disk since the last save, show a diff and let the user choose how to resolve the mismatch

items.title: LSP restart persistence omits state required by its own rules
items.statement: The behavior requires a persisted crash budget and backoff state, but the implementation key stores only server config, capabilities, status, and restart count. The crash-window definition, backoff deadline, reset reason, attached-document set, and atomicity of replay are absent.
items.impact: Restarting PM can reset or misapply the budget, create a restart storm, or falsely disclose a session as current after only partial document replay.

evidence.exact_quote:
On crash, `/transport` loss, or `/sync-loss` restart, PM recreates the host-aware LSP session and replays all currently attached documents for that session/root in deterministic URI order.
- Automatic restart uses the persisted restart budget and backoff state; after the bounded crash budget is exhausted, the session remains `Degraded` until user retry, and a user-initiated restart resets the budget/backoff counters.
- Each host-aware LSP session keeps a bounded protocol/state trace buffer for operational/debug inspection only, not canonical app history; the surfaced trace fields include session key, root, current state, last error, restart attempt/backoff, and a recent protocol trace reveal action.

Implementation spec:
- key: `lsp_server_state.v1:{host_id}:{server_id}:{root_hash}`
- stores: server config, capabilities snapshot, last known status, and restart count
- recovery path: on session restore, restart LSP servers using the persisted config
- persisted restart counts survive reconnects so budget enforcement and degraded-state disclosure remain stable after restart

items.title: Corrupt-record skip rule lacks a safe resynchronization algorithm
items.statement: The problem table mandates skipping a corrupt record, but it does not distinguish a payload CRC failure from a damaged length/header or active-tail truncation. In a length-prefixed stream, a corrupted framing field can make the next record boundary unknowable.
items.impact: A builder may scan arbitrary bytes as records, discard valid later data, or loop indefinitely while claiming recovery succeeded.

evidence.exact_quote: | **seglog corruption or partial write** | Append-only with flush and last-complete-record recovery. CRC32 per record is mandatory; validate on every read; corrupt record -> skip + recovery event. |

items.title: Phase-one acceptance can pass without mandatory CRC integrity
items.statement: The implementation order and phase-one acceptance require append/read order but omit CRC generation, verification, corrupt-tail handling, and recovery events, despite the same source declaring CRC32 mandatory.
items.impact: The storage foundation can be certified complete while violating a mandatory correctness requirement that later components depend on.

evidence.exact_quote:
- **Phase 1 -- seglog foundation**
  Build first: app data root resolution, directory creation (`storage/seglog`, `storage/redb`, `storage/jsonl`, `storage/tantivy`), and seglog writer only (envelope format, seq, flush, optional rotation by size/day). No projectors, no redb.
  **Exit criterion:** We can append events and read them back (by tailing or reading the segment file).

items.title: Permission snapshots have an enforceable immutable lineage boundary
items.statement: The source assigns schema ownership externally, gives a durable key and attempt link, requires write-before-dispatch, and makes later changes create a new snapshot and attempt lineage. This is sufficiently explicit for authority and historical replay.
items.impact: Permission changes cannot retroactively rewrite what an earlier attempt was authorized to do.

evidence.exact_quote:
**Canonical storage binding:**
- durable family: `permission_snapshot_record.v1:{project_id}:{snapshot_id}`
- immutable link from attempt state: `attempt_record.permission_snapshot_id`
- projector/query fields MAY cache `blocked_family`, `approval_scope_key`, `approval_target_ref`, and `revalidation_required` for indexing, but they MUST NOT redefine the nested snapshot schema locally

**Rules:**
1. The snapshot record is written before the corresponding attempt becomes durable/dispatchable.
2. The snapshot payload is immutable after creation. Later approval or policy changes create a new snapshot and a new attempt lineage entry; they do not rewrite the old one.
3. Snapshot retention follows attempt lineage and any stronger preservation/hold rule.
4. storage-plan MUST reference the owner-doc schema instead of embedding a competing schema copy.

items.title: Post-action web results can poison action-free cache reads
items.statement: Action-bearing reads bypass lookup but their final content is explicitly cacheable for later action-free requests keyed by URL/formats/adapter. The cache identity omits action sequence, account, auth realm, cookie/session state, and visibility scope.
items.impact: User-specific or state-mutated content can be served as a generic hit to a different operation or identity, leaking data and returning semantically false page state.

evidence.exact_quote:
The PM-owned web cache contract must preserve two-phase lookup, state vocabulary, and per-project cache sizing.
- Cache routing must skip read-time cache for requests with actions, may still store the post-action result, and must preserve PM-cache precedence over Firecrawl cache with diff-reuse audit states.
- Web cache persistence is per-project with a 500 MB default cache budget, per-operation TTL defaults, LRU eviction for bounded storage, stable cache key ordering, and change detection persistence for future `change_tracking` comparison.
- Each cache entry stores `cache_key: string` as the hash of `(url, formats, adapter_id)`, `url: string` as normalized `URL`, `formats_requested: string[]`, `adapter_id`, `content_hash`, `content_ref: string` as a pointer to cached content and not inline content, `metadata: { title?: string, status_code?: number, content_type?: string, content_length?: number }`, `fetched_at` as ISO time, `expires_at` as `fetched_at` plus TTL, `access_count`, and `last_accessed_at`; eviction is LRU and TTL-driven.

items.title: Two-phase cache lookup has no unambiguous index contract
items.statement: The durable key hashes adapter ID, but lookup before adapter selection uses only URL and formats hash and later validates adapter ID. The source does not define a secondary index, behavior when several adapter entries exist, hash collision handling, or normalization and ordering of formats.
items.impact: Implementations can select different entries, treat a valid alternative-adapter entry as a miss, or overwrite colliding variants.

evidence.exact_quote: Each cache entry stores `cache_key: string` as the hash of `(url, formats, adapter_id)`, `url: string` as normalized `URL`, `formats_requested: string[]`, `adapter_id`, `content_hash`, `content_ref: string` as a pointer to cached content and not inline content, `metadata: { title?: string, status_code?: number, content_type?: string, content_length?: number }`, `fetched_at` as ISO time, `expires_at` as `fetched_at` plus TTL, `access_count`, and `last_accessed_at`; eviction is LRU and TTL-driven.

items.title: Projection trust does not grant mutation authority
items.statement: The contract explicitly separates freshness/health from action authority and mandates a direct-record fallback plus trust-aware action gating. This is a strong negative constraint for misleading projection-backed GUI states.
items.impact: A fresh-looking read model cannot by itself authorize a sensitive action when projection trust is degraded.

evidence.exact_quote:
Behavioral rules:
- Projection freshness is not the same thing as action authority.
- Projection-backed surfaces must degrade to direct-record views when trust drops.
- Runtime-artifact projections must be rebuildable from canonical seglog events.

Permission carry-through:
- action gating must respect projection trust before surfacing mutation actions

items.title: Cache bypass options conflate read and write behavior
items.statement: `max_age_seconds: 0` and `store: false` both record `bypassed` and suppress a cached read, but the prose does not state whether max-age zero may still store the fresh result or whether `store:false` suppresses only this write. The later general rule says post-action results are cacheable, creating another precedence question.
items.impact: Callers cannot predict whether a forced-refresh request warms the cache or whether an explicit no-store request can be overridden.

evidence.exact_quote:
If request includes `actions`, skip cache entirely (always fresh-execute). Actions modify page state, so cache lookup only applies to action-free requests.
- Cache STORE still applies to the final result after actions execute; the post-action content is cacheable for future action-free requests to the same normalized `URL`.
- Cache bypass: when `cache_policy.max_age_seconds: 0` or `cache_policy.store: false`, storage records `cache_state: "bypassed"` and does not serve a cached read for that operation.
- If cache is enabled and an entry exists within TTL, return the cached result with `cache_state: "hit"` and skip provider execution UNLESS the request includes `actions` or the post-selection `adapter_id` validation fails.

synthesis.overall_assessment: The assigned storage span has strong authority boundaries for seglog/projectors, immutable permission snapshots, projection trust, multi-store roles, and deterministic segment naming. It is not build-assurance complete: 39 gaps remain, dominated by incomplete state machines, cache isolation, corrupt-log recovery ambiguity, missing binary/parser bounds, unsafe destructive/cache concurrency, and generic PlanUnit acceptance criteria that validate preservation rather than behavior.
highest_risk_clusters: Post-action web content can enter an action-free cache without account/session/action scope.
Corrupt seglog handling is not deterministic across payload CRC failure, framing corruption, immutable closed segments, and active-tail truncation.
Runtime/worktree, identity, TODO revision, concern, account-pressure, and lane/worktree lifecycle records lack complete lineage or state-machine contracts.
Regex index completeness, binary validation, crash-atomic publication, cache collision handling, and remote dirty-file coverage lack falsifiable adversarial oracles.
Sensitive/destructive behavior including main-project fallback, cache eviction, clear-all, and visual-module replay lacks sufficient safety boundaries.
cross_segment_seams: Phase-one seglog acceptance omits the mandatory CRC behavior formalized later by SP-025.
The prologue's corrupt-record skip rule conflicts with SP-028's truncate-only-corrupt-tail rule.
The web cache durable key includes adapter_id while pre-selection lookup excludes it, and post-action storage omits identity/action scope.
Projection trust axes are well separated, but SP-006 does not turn them into a testable action-gating matrix.
SP-030's immutable-record rule conflicts with an undefined updated_at_utc field.
synthesis.builder_discretion_assessment: Unbounded in all 39 gap items; bounded or absent only where the source supplies an explicit authority, immutability, or deterministic ordering rule.
unknowns: Whether external owner documents close some field schemas cannot be established in this blind single-excerpt phase.
Whether migration/index validators test behavioral semantics rather than source preservation is not established by the assigned excerpt.
The assignment-record hash is bound from the dispatch intent; no separate assignment-record file was referenced for direct hash verification.
